## What I verified independently

**Hashes.** All eight pinned source/input digests recomputed and match `approval-inputs.json` exactly. `copy-receipt.json.plan_sha256` equals the actual `plan.json` digest.

**The eight copies.** Rehashed all eight `.tar` files in `.run/actor291_release_20261015/archive-offload/offloaded/`. Every sha256 and size matches both `plan.json` and the receipt; remote paths match; eight unique paths; `scp_exit: 0` on all eight; sizes sum to exactly 591,301,120; the directory holds exactly eight files and is ignored via `.gitignore:212`.

**Removal safety.** The shell's inlined core (`offload.sh:44-103`) is byte-identical to `offload.py` (clean diff). The file contains exactly one `.unlink()`, inside an eight-entry loop guarded by `assert len(entries)==8` and the byte sum. No glob, iterdir, rmtree, shutil, `rm`, `rmi`, `image rm`, `prune`, `systemctl` or restart anywhere. Per entry: exact normalized parent, not in PROTECTED (5 names), pattern narrowed to `.tar` dates 10.02–10.13 (tightened from `1[0-4]`), `str(logical)==entry['path']` kills traversal, non-symlink, `S_ISREG`, dev/ino/size/mtime pinned, `O_NOFOLLOW` open, `fstat` both before and after the digest, final `lstat` + symlink recheck. Whole batch validated before the first unlink, then revalidated immediately before each one.

**Guards.** Both modules raise on `not __debug__` above all logic — the rerun of the `-O` test confirms both fail before logic. The shell unsets `PYTHONOPTIMIZE`/`PYTHONSTARTUP`, pins the hostname three times, and holds the existing `DEPLOY.lock` on fd 8 via `flock -n` for the whole script, inherited by every heredoc child.

**Before/after symmetry.** Health block lines 9-26 is byte-identical to 130-147; protected+inventory 29-41 identical to 113-125. All four protected dict literals equal `protected-hashes.json` (16 files). Both inventory assertions equal `image-inventory.json` (containerd 201, docker 47) using read-only list commands.

**K3s scope.** I fetched the official `v1.36.4+k3s1` `watcher.go`; its digest matches `k3s-source-evidence.json` exactly, and the missing-file branch is byte-identical to the recorded text. That branch only does `delete(w.filesCache, key)` + `syncCache` + return; `pruneCache` prunes cache entries only; there is no image-delete call in the file. Combined with the runtime inventory guard, archive removal cannot delete loaded images.
